rationale: Published studies delineating SMAD2-related Loeys-Dietz syndrome 6 support the hypothesis that thoracic aortic aneurysm occurs in a majority of symptomatic adult carriers (e.g., Cannaerts et al. reported thoracic aortic aneurysm in carriers, ~10 cases), while younger individuals or those presenting early often display either normal aortic calibers or congenital heart disease (CHD) with laterality defects rather than early childhood aortic aneurysms/dissections, confirming a late-onset/progressive vascular phenotype.

evidence.text: SMAD2 (likely) pathogenic variant carriers display thoracic aortic aneurysm in a majority of examined cases, delineating the arterial phenotype across multiple families.

evidence.text: SMAD2 pathogenic variants manifest as two distinct presentations: complex CHD with or without laterality defects in pediatric/fetal cases, and a late-onset vascular phenotype characterized by thoracic arterial/aortic root aneurysms in adults.

source.title: Variable cardiovascular phenotypes associated with SMAD2 pathogenic variants
source.quote: Our data suggest two distinct phenotypes associated with pathogenic variants in SMAD2: complex CHD with or without laterality defects and other congenital anomalies, and a late-onset vascular phenotype characterized by arterial aneurysms with connective tissue abnormalities.

evidence.text: In a 25-year institutional cohort of 103 Loeys-Dietz syndrome patients (types 1 to 5), no SMAD2 pathogenic variants were identified, illustrating that SMAD2-associated LDS (LDS6) remains very rare compared to LDS1-5.

source.title: Characterization of Arterial Aneurysms in Loeys-Dietz Syndrome

new_directions.question_text: What is the penetrance and age of onset of thoracic aortic aneurysm in asymptomatic pediatric and adolescent SMAD2 variant carriers followed longitudinally?
new_directions.rationale: Because younger patients often present with either congenital heart defects or completely normal aortic roots prior to adulthood, prospective surveillance is required to establish the true age-dependent penetrance of aortic disease.

new_directions.question_text: Do SMAD2 missense versus loss-of-function/truncating variants correlate with the dichotomy between late-onset aneurysmal disease versus early complex CHD/laterality defects?
new_directions.rationale: Granadillo et al. observed two divergent phenotypic classes; evaluating genotype-phenotype correlations could clarify whether specific functional impacts drive early vs late cardiovascular presentations.
